pr_title: PRO-9314: Add support for files pretty URLs in static builds

gold.summary: Resolving relative attachment URLs using req.get('host') relies on the untrusted Host header. An attacker supplying a crafted Host header can redirect the server-side streamProxy request to an arbitrary host (SSRF).
notes: faulty proxyUrl construction using untrusted Host header passed to streamProxy

finding.title: Server-side request forgery via attacker-controlled Host header in proxyUrl
finding.body: The proxyUrl for attachments is assembled using req.get('host'), so the host portion of the URL sent to streamProxy is whatever the client supplies in the Host header. When a request arrives with a forged Host header pointing at an external address, the server fetches that external address instead of the expected local attachment source, enabling SSRF.

pr_title: fix: propagate dispatcher origin to composed interceptors

gold.summary: The dispatch wrapper only populates the origin from self[kUrl] when opts.origin is absent, preserving any caller-provided origin. This allows caller-controlled origin metadata to reach origin-dependent interceptors such as cache and deduplication, enabling cross-origin cache poisoning and state leakage.

finding.title: Caller-supplied origin bypasses dispatcher origin resolution

Any caller that passes an arbitrary origin string can therefore make downstream interceptors like cache and dedup key on a spoofed origin, leaking or poisoning entries across real origins.

pr_title: fix: inherit iframe sandbox flags in windows opened on the OpenURL navigation path

gold.summary: The `initiator->GetParent()` check restricts sandbox enforcement to child frames, skipping top-level frames. Consequently, windows opened via `OpenURLFromTab` from a sandboxed top-level frame fail to inherit the opener's sandbox restrictions and can bypass popup blocking.

pr_title: Further restrict DNS wildcards in name constraint matching

gold.summary: Evaluating permittedSubtrees using DNSConstraint::matches applies wildcard overlap semantics rather than subtree containment. Consequently, a wildcard SAN like *.example.com is wrongly permitted by a narrower constraint such as bar.example.com even though the wildcard can expand to names outside that permitted subtree.
notes: faulty call evaluating name constraints using wildcard overlap matching
implementation of the method the faulty call relies on, which implements wildcard overlap matching

finding.title: Permitted DNS subtree check accepts wildcard SANs that can escape the constraint
finding.body: The permittedSubtrees evaluation calls DNSConstraint::matches, which was designed for wildcard-overlap checks, not for deciding whether a name is contained inside a subtree. A certificate with SAN *.example.com is therefore accepted under a constraint of bar.example.com, because the wildcard-overlap logic sees that the pattern could match bar.example.com, even though *.example.com can also match names such as foo.other.example.com that are outside the permitted subtree.

pr_title: SQL: Guard fill resampling in MSSQL, PostgreSQL and MySQL

gold.summary: `stripSQLComments` strips `#` comments using the naive regex `#[^\n]*` (`reHashComment`), which matches `#` characters inside quoted strings and JSON paths, truncating queries and causing SQL syntax errors.
notes: faulty regex replacement stripping # comments regardless of quotes

finding.title: Hash comment removal ignores quoting context
finding.body: The reHashComment regex `#[^\n]*` is applied indiscriminately, so any `#` character, even one inside a single- or double-quoted string or a JSON path, starts a comment match. For example, a query containing `SELECT '#not_a_comment'` becomes `SELECT '` after stripSQLComments, producing an unterminated string and a SQL syntax error. The trigger condition is any interpolated MySQL query that contains a `#` character inside a quoted literal or JSON extraction expression.

pr_title: fix(mcp): close stdio sessions on their owning loop to avoid cross-task cancel-scope error (#3379)

gold.summary: get_session() assumes any existing session or in-flight creation on a different event loop is stale and evicts or cancels it. When concurrent synchronous calls run on separate event loops for the same server and scope, they cancel each other's active sessions or in-flight initialization, aborting tool execution with CancelledError.
notes: faulty eviction of established sessions created on other running event loops
faulty eviction and cancellation of in-flight sessions created on other running event loops

finding.title: Concurrent sync callers on different loops evict each other's live sessions
finding.body: get_session() treats a session or pending future as stale whenever its recorded loop differs from the caller's running loop, without checking whether that other loop is still running. If two synchronous threads each call the MCP tool for the same server/scope on separate event loops, the second caller's get_session() will pop the first caller's session or cancel its in-flight future, so the first caller's tool invocation fails with CancelledError. The pool should only evict when the owning loop is actually closed or not running, not merely different.

When concurrent synchronous calls run on separate event loops for the same server and scope, they cancel each other's active sessions or in-flight initialization, aborting tool execution with CancelledError.

finding.title: Session pool lock is not held while awaiting session creation
finding.body: The code drops the asyncio lock before awaiting the session-creation coroutine and then reacquires it to store the result, so two tasks in the same loop can both observe an empty entry and start duplicate stdio subprocesses for the same server/scope. One of the resulting sessions is orphaned and never closed, leaking a child process and its pipes. The lock or a per-key future should be held across the whole creation path.

gold.summary: get_session() assumes any existing session or in-flight creation on a different event loop is stale and evicts or cancels it. When concurrent synchronous calls run on separate event loops for the same server and scope, they cancel each other's active sessions or in-flight initialization, aborting tool execution with CancelledError.

finding.title: Eviction on loop mismatch also tears down sessions for a server that is merely being rediscovered
finding.body: When the same server name is re-registered with a fresh configuration (for example after a hot reload or config refresh) while an old session is still alive on a different loop, get_session() again keys only on server/scope and loop identity, so it evicts and cancels the established session even though the old loop is healthy. This is a different trigger from concurrent callers: a single sequential re-registration causes the same destructive eviction. The pool needs to distinguish a genuinely stale loop from a configuration-generation change.

finding.title: Decimal average duration breaks deadline arithmetic
finding.body: The database query used to compute the average task duration can yield a Decimal because the SQL column is numeric. Passing that Decimal directly as the seconds argument to timedelta raises TypeError, so any deadline evaluation where the average duration is returned as Decimal fails at runtime. The trigger is simply an AverageRuntimeDeadline being evaluated when the stored duration is a Decimal rather than an int or float.

The evaluation should handle an empty result set explicitly, either by returning no deadline or by raising a descriptive exception.

finding.title: Negative average duration produces invalid past deadline
finding.body: When the stored average duration is negative, adding it to the current time creates a deadline in the past, causing the task to be marked as immediately missed. The code does not validate that avg_duration_seconds is non-negative before constructing the deadline interval.
